title: Priority Spine & Release Lanes: Translating Strategic Goals into Initiative Delivery Contracts
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Teams are launching initiatives that are loosely aligned to company goals, creating uneven capacity pulls, duplicated work, and unclear escalation paths. Objective: Define a single "Priority Spine" that sequences company-level objectives into explicit "Release Lanes" (timeboxed initiative delivery contracts) with decision checkpoints, capacity commitments, and rollback/fallback triggers. Scope: company-level OKRs + top 15 cross-functional initiatives for Q2-Q3 2026. Deliverables: (1) a Priority Spine document mapping each objective to 1–3 initiatives with owners and success metrics; (2) a Release Lanes template (commitment contract) that each initiative signs: milestones, capacity slice, risk level, fallback model; (3) an escalation/runbook for trade-offs and resource reallocation; (4) a lightweight dashboard in Console showing lane health and commitment utilization.
acceptance_criteria: - Priority Spine published and reviewed by execs and all initiative owners; - Release Lanes template adopted by >90% of top 15 initiatives with an explicit owner and capacity commitment documented; - Dashboard prototype shows live progress for at least 6 initiatives and flags <3 blockers with suggested mitigations; - Two cross-functional tabletop runbooks executed to validate escalation/rollback behavior.
updates: 2026-03-01 — Ticket created. Kickoff scheduled with PM leads, Eng, Design, and Finance. Initial stakeholder list assembled.

2026-03-03 — Workshop with exec sponsors (CTO, VP Product). Decision: Priority Spine will be authoritative for resource arbitration during Q2. Asked to prototype Release Lanes for 6 pilot initiatives.

2026-03-04 — Spoke with Capacity Planning (Infra ops). Constraint: dedicated GPU pool capacity is projected tight in May; recommended including explicit capacity slices and fallback models in lane contracts.
2026-03-05 — Draft Release Lanes template created; reviewed by Legal for contractual language (no formal legal signoff required). Prepared initial Confluence doc and Drive folder.
2026-03-06 — Design reviewed initial dashboard wireframes. Feedback: surface delta vs committed capacity, and an 'impact severity' heatband. Design will supply assets by 2026-03-10.

2026-03-07 — Engineering raised a blocker: current rollout tooling lacks native per-lane throttles; agreed to scope a small runtime feature spike (ENG-24567) to add a lane-level throttle toggle for canary/fallback.
2026-03-08 — PM triage: nominated 6 pilot initiatives across Eng, Console, Dedicated, Optimize, and Private. Owners notified; asked to complete lane contract draft by 2026-03-15.
2026-03-09 — Exec review calendar invite sent for 2026-03-18. Action items: owners to attach PRDs, success metrics, and capacity commitments prior to review.
next_steps: 1) Finalize Release Lanes template by 2026-03-10; 2) Owners to complete contracts by 2026-03-15; 3) Exec review 2026-03-18 and decision on resource arbitration policy; 4) Dashboard prototype delivery by 2026-03-24.
notes: Trade-offs considered: stricter spine enforcement reduces local team autonomy but improves predictability for capacity and cost. We will pilot with 6 initiatives to limit risk and iterate on the governance language. Finance requested explicit cost impact lines per lane; will add a 'cost delta' field to the contract template. Design requested real examples to validate dashboard affordances. Engineering is prioritizing a small feature spike to support lane-level runtime controls; this is scoped as a dependency (ENG-24567).
